evidence: src/application/use-cases/CreateTaskUseCase.ts and src/application/use-cases/ListProjectTasksUseCase.ts both turn raw status strings into statuses with the domain's `parseTaskStatus`, so status validation lives in one place.
src/application/use-cases/CreateProjectUseCase.ts, CreateTaskUseCase.ts and CreateUserUseCase.ts all get new ids from `this.ids.next()` through the `IdGenerator` port.

src/application/use-cases/AssignTaskUseCase.ts, CompleteTaskUseCase.ts, CreateTaskUseCase.ts and ListProjectTasksUseCase.ts all return task results through `toTaskDto` and raise `NotFoundError('Task'|'Project', id)` from `../errors/ApplicationError` when an entity is missing.

Every class follows the same shape: dependencies passed in through the constructor, plus one `execute(input): Promise<Dto>` method. Business changes are left to the entity's own methods (`task.assignTo`, `task.markDone`).

src/application/use-cases/CreateTaskUseCase.ts sets `status: input.status === undefined ? 'todo' : ...` itself. This is a minor case of entity default logic sitting in the use case, but it is not duplicated anywhere.

They use the module's abstractions the same way throughout. Persistence always goes through the domain repository interfaces. New ids always come from the `IdGenerator` port. Every result is returned through the DTO mappers (`toTaskDto`, `toProjectDto`, `toUserDto`). Missing entities always raise the shared `NotFoundError`. Status strings are always parsed by the domain's `parseTaskStatus`, and due dates by `DueDate.fromString`, so that validation is not written twice. The repeated 'load the entity, then throw if it is null' pattern is ordinary use-case orchestration, not a copied business rule. Using `UnknownAssigneeError` in `AssignTaskUseCase` is a deliberate, different error meaning, not an inconsistency. One small note: `CreateTaskUseCase` sets the default status to `'todo'` itself. That default arguably belongs inside the `Task` entity, but it appears only once, so nothing is duplicated. No file splits off into an unrelated concern or skips the module's ports.
